title: Developer Experience docs playbook: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs site ops, top support issues & fixes
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Playbook for producing and maintaining Developer Experience documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, canonical API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for top support issues.
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the conventions, templates, and operational procedures the Developer Experience (DevEx) team uses to author, review, publish, and maintain SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, and the docs site. It also captures the top support issues we see for SDKs and docs and the canonical fixes to reduce toil. The audience is DevEx writers, SDK owners, triage engineers, and Docs ops.

Goals
- Provide consistent, high-quality SDK and quickstart docs that get developers to a working integration in under 15 minutes.
- Reduce support volume by surfacing canonical fixes and clear troubleshooting guidance.
- Keep docs evergreen through a lightweight operating procedure for review, publish, and deprecation.

Scope
- SDK guides (Python, JavaScript, Go), quickstarts and templates, canonical API examples (curl, HTTP, SDK snippets), docs site operating procedures (content lifecycle), and a short list of top support issues with remediation.

Ownership & SLAs
- Primary owner: eng-developer-experience (DevEx)
- Secondary owners: eng-platform (docs infra), eng-sre (site reliability for docs hosting)
- Review SLA: docs authored must have a peer review within 3 business days.
- Publish SLA: minor fixes published within 2 business days; new quickstarts shipped within 10 business days after review.

Doc Types & Templates
1) SDK Guide (Canonical template)
- Purpose: Reference + quickstart for language SDK (API surface, auth, common patterns, errors, migration notes).
- Recommended sections (in order):
  1. Title + short 1-line summary
  2. Getting started (install, auth)
  3. Minimal quickstart (copy-paste runnable example)
  4. Common patterns (streaming, batching, retries, rate limiting)
  5. Error handling and troubleshooting table
  6. Advanced topics (caching, performance tuning, pagination)
  7. Migration notes (for breaking changes)
  8. API reference link and changelog notes
- Required metadata: title, version, last_reviewed, owner_team, compatibility (API + runtime versions).

2) Quickstart / Tutorial Template
- Goal: get a developer from zero to sample-app in ~10 minutes.
- Sections: overview, prerequisites, install, configuration (env vars), minimal app, run & test, next steps, teardown.
- Checklist before publish: runnable locally, example keys are expo/placeholder, CI smoke-test passes, suggested time-to-complete (<= 15m) included.

3) API Example Snippets
- Provide canonical examples for:
  - Text generation (sync + streaming)
  - Chat (messages + function/tool calling)
  - Embeddings (single + batch)
  - Reranking / similarity search pattern
- Each example must include: curl, Python (requests or official SDK), JavaScript (fetch or official SDK) and expected response shape.
- Keep examples short (< 20 lines) and link to full examples in the repo.

Canonical SDK Quickstart (Python)
```
# pip install redwood-inference
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")
resp = client.generate("Write a 2-sentence product summary for Redwood Inference")
print(resp.text)
```

Canonical API curl example
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Summarize our platform in two lines"}'
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (content lifecycle)
- Authoring: create a draft in the correct space and attach the required metadata fields.
- Peer review: assign 1 reviewer from DevEx + 1 from owning SDK team for API changes. Reviews must add inline comments and an approval comment on the page.
- Security review: any sample that includes networking, auth patterns, or addresses PII must be reviewed by Security (add reviewer).
- Publishing: Docs owner pushes the page from draft -> in_review -> published. The DevEx release manager tags release notes.
- Evergreen checks: run the docs site smoke-test weekly (CI job docs/smoke-test) that validates that canonical curl + SDK snippets return 200 and expected schema.
- Deprecation: when SDK methods or API endpoints are deprecated, add a deprecation banner at the top, update migration notes, and schedule removal at EoL date.

Review & Release Workflow (numbered)
1. Author drafts page and assigns reviewers (DevEx + SDK owner).
2. CI: lint + snippet-tests run.
3. Reviewers resolve comments; author updates doc.
4. Author marks page ready; reviewers approve.
5. Release manager publishes and records page in release notes and the weekly docs digest.

Docs Quality Gates (required checks)
- Examples are runnable (CI smoke-test).
- All code snippets use official SDK when possible.
- No hard-coded production API keys; placeholders must be used.
- Accessibility: images include alt text, headings follow hierarchical order.

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes
Note: these issues represent recurring triage tickets from support and SRE (2025-2026). Each entry: symptom, root cause, canonical fix, detection, owner.

1) Issue: SDK auth failures with client-side env var usage
- Symptom: 401 returned intermittently in builds / CI; local run works.
- Root cause: CI agents use a different env var name (REDWOOD_API_TOKEN vs REDWOOD_API_KEY) or token not exported to subprocesses.
- Canonical fix: Standardize examples on REDWOOD_API_KEY; update CI template snippets to ensure export (export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...). Add a troubleshooting bullet in SDK guide.
- Detection: CI smoke-test failing for example-runner; automated alert posted to #devex-smoke.
- Owner: eng-developer-experience + eng-infra (CI templates).

2) Issue: Streaming examples causing partial outputs / stalled clients
- Symptom: client receives initial chunk then stalls indefinitely.
- Root cause: consumers using blocking HTTP client without streaming support or missing chunked transfer-handling in proxies.
- Canonical fix: Provide non-streaming fallback examples; add explicit instructions for configuring popular proxies (nginx: proxy_buffering off; haproxy: option http-server-close). Add test cases in smoke-test for streaming.
- Detection: Sentry alerts for stalled requests; manual repro steps saved in ticket.
- Owner: eng-developer-experience + eng-sre.

3) Issue: Model mismatch after minor version rollouts
- Symptom: customers see semantic changes in outputs after service upgrade.
- Root cause: rollout applied a model variant with different prompt template/temperature default and no pinned version in docs examples.
- Canonical fix: Always include model_version in quickstarts and examples (e.g., model: redwood-1.0.3). Add a template line: \"Recommended: pin model_version during tutorials to avoid surprises.\"
- Detection: Post-deploy eval alerts from Redwood Optimize and customer tickets.
- Owner: eng-developer-experience + research/applied-ml.

4) Issue: Embeddings batch size OOM in customer integrations
- Symptom: Customers get OOM or 500 errors when sending large batch embeddings requests.
- Root cause: customers sending too-large batches; default SDK helper used an aggressive auto-batch parameter.
- Canonical fix: Update SDK helper defaults to conservative batch_size=64 and document memory/performance tradeoffs in embeddings guide. Add failure-mode guidance and exponential backoff sample.
- Detection: Error budget spikes in embeddings routes; alerting rule embeddings_5xx_rate.
- Owner: eng-developer-experience + eng-serving-runtime.

Quick Troubleshooting Table (example)
| Symptom | Quick check | Likely fix | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| 401 auth | Is REDWOOD_API_KEY set? Is key expired? | Rotate key; update env export; use placeholders in docs | DevEx + Customer Success |
| Partial stream | Is client using streaming-capable HTTP lib? Is proxy buffering off? | Provide non-stream example; proxy config guidance | DevEx + SRE |
| Unexpected outputs | Was model pinned in example? | Pin model_version in quickstart; add migration note | DevEx + ML Research |
| Embedding OOMs | Batch size? memory footprint? | Lower batch_size; use cursor/pagination | DevEx + Serving Runtime |

Publishing checklist (pre-publish)
- [ ] Page filled with required metadata (title, author, owner_team, status, created_at).
- [ ] Peer review completed (reviewers added).
- [ ] CI smoke-tests green for snippets.
- [ ] Security checklist (if applicable) completed.
- [ ] Release manager notified.

Post-publish maintenance
- Weekly: CI smoke-test run; failures create a ticket in the docs backlog.
- Quarterly: Content review for high-traffic pages (last_updated > 90 days triggers review).
- Deprecation window: 90-day notice for breaking changes in examples, with migration guide.

Appendix: Useful CLI commands and snippets
- Run docs site smoke tests: `ci/docs/smoke-test.sh`
- Lint examples: `npm run docs:lint` or `python -m rdocs.lint`
- Run canonical example runner (local):
```
./scripts/run-canonical-examples.sh --only python, curl
```

Contact & escalation
- Primary contact: eng-developer-experience (Slack: #devex, PagerDuty: DevEx-oncall)
- Escalation: raise P1s to eng-sre and product manager for incidents impacting docs availability or canonical examples failing.
